entry: Banded variety of [[Chalcedony]], a microcrystalline form of silica. Agate has alternating bands of differently colored chalcedony and often contains visible [[Quartz|quartz]] crystals. Most agates form as nodules within volcanic rock. The processes that produce the banding are not well understood, and agate has never been made synthetically. It has been used as a gemstone in jewelry for thousands of years and is popular with collectors. Many duller agates sold commercially are artificially treated to enhance their color.

English writer of mystery and detective fiction, known as the Queen of Crime. She wrote 66 [[Detective fiction|detective]] novels and 14 short-story collections, including those featuring Hercule Poirot, Tommy and Tuppence, and Miss Marple. After six consecutive rejections, *The Mysterious Affair at Styles*, which introduced Poirot, was published in 1920. Her play *The Mousetrap* opened in London's West End on November 25, 1952, and holds the world record for the longest initial run, with more than 27,500 performances by 2018. She is the best-selling novelist of all time, with more than two billion copies of her books sold; *And Then There Were None* alone sold about 100 million copies. Her 1930 marriage to the [[Archaeology|archaeologist]] Max Mallowan took her on excavations in the Middle East, which informed her fiction. In 1971 she was made a Dame by [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]].

Genus of over 200 species of succulent monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas. Most species form large rosettes of thick, fleshy leaves with sharp marginal teeth and an extremely sharp terminal spine. Most agaves are monocarpic: each rosette flowers once, on a tall stalk that can reach 12 metres (40 feet), and then dies, although many species produce suckers that become new plants. Some agave species are known as century plants, and some varieties can live 60 years before flowering. Agave leaves store water, and the plants are widely grown as ornamentals in hot, dry climates. About 75% of species occur in [[Mexico]], where agaves have been used for food and fiber since pre-Columbian times. Tequila and mezcal are distilled from agave, and sisal and henequen fibers are used for rope.

Estimated age of the Earth, 4.54 ± 0.05 billion years. The estimate rests on radiometric dating of [[Meteorite|meteorites]], whose ages are approached by those of the oldest terrestrial material and lunar samples. The oldest dated [[Zircon|zircon]] crystals, from the Jack Hills of Western Australia, are at least 4.404 billion years old. Calcium–aluminium-rich inclusions, the oldest known solid matter in the Solar System, are 4.5673 ± 0.00016 billion years old.

Minimum age at which a person is legally competent to consent to sexual activity. Sexual activity with a younger person is treated as [[Child sexual abuse|child sexual abuse]] or [[Statutory rape|statutory rape]], with the younger person regarded as the victim, although some jurisdictions have exceptions for close-in-age partners. The term rarely appears in statutes, which usually set the age below which sexual activity is illegal. Nearly all jurisdictions set the age between 14 and 18 years. Cuba sets it at 12; Argentina, Niger and Western Sahara at 13; and Bahrain at 21, while 14 Muslim states allow consent only through marriage. Laws may also vary by type of act, gender or position of trust. Many grey areas remain, including conflicts between federal and state laws in the United States.

Cosmological time since the [[Big Bang]], estimated at 13.8 billion years. The estimate uses Big Bang models and data from the Planck project, which measured the [[Cosmic microwave background|cosmic microwave background]]. A second approach, based on the distances and velocities of a ladder of stars, gives slightly different values for the Hubble constant, but its range also lies within the estimate for the oldest observed star. Through most of the 19th century and into the early 20th, most scientists presumed the universe was steady state and eternal.

Chemical herbicide and defoliant used by the United States and South Vietnam in the [[Vietnam War]]. Used in Operation Ranch Hand from 1962 to 1971, it was a mixture of equal parts 2,4-D and 2,4,5-T that contained trace amounts of the dioxin TCDD. Exposure is linked to birth defects, cancers, cardiovascular disease and diabetes, though causality remains incompletely established. Over 7,700,000 acres (3,100,000 ha) of tropical forest in Vietnam were defoliated, causing enormous environmental damage.

Behavior aimed at opposing or attacking someone or something, often with intent to cause harm. Direct aggression involves physical or verbal behavior intended to harm a person, while indirect aggression targets the social relations of an individual or group. In the social and behavioral sciences it is commonly defined as an action that delivers something unpleasant to another person. Humans show two subtypes: controlled, instrumental aggression aimed at a goal, and reactive, impulsive aggression that is often a response to provocation. Interdisciplinary researchers describe it as a set of mechanisms shaped by [[Evolution|evolution]] to gain or defend resources, often driven by fear, frustration, anger or dominance. Aggression differs from assertiveness, although the terms are often used interchangeably, and researchers continue to debate the relative roles of biology and environment.

Semiaquatic venomous pit viper of the southeastern United States, also called the cottonmouth. It is the largest species in its [[Genus|genus]]; adults commonly exceed 80 cm (31 in) in total length, and a record specimen measured 189.2 cm (74.5 in). It lives in or near slow-moving, shallow lakes, streams and marshes and is a capable swimmer. When threatened it coils and gapes, exposing the white lining of its mouth, a display to which many of its common names refer. It may bite when threatened or handled, and its bite is painful and potentially fatal. A 2014 [[DNA]]-based study recognized two species: the northern cottonmouth (*Agkistrodon piscivorus*) and the Florida cottonmouth (*Agkistrodon conanti*).

Belgian-born French filmmaker, artist and photographer. Her work employed location shooting and nonprofessional actors, unconventional for 1950s French cinema. Her feature debut, *La Pointe Courte* (1955), was followed by *Cléo from 5 to 7* (1962) and *Vagabond* (1985), which won a Golden Lion at the 1985 Venice Film Festival. Her documentaries include *The Gleaners and I* (2000) and *Faces Places* (2017). In 2015 she received an Honorary Palme d'Or at the [[Cannes Film Festival]], becoming the first female filmmaker to win the award, and in 2017 she became the first female director to win an Academy Honorary Award. [[Martin Scorsese]] described her as one of the gods of cinema.

Paraphyletic infraphylum of jawless fish within the subphylum Vertebrata. Its living members, the [[Lamprey|lampreys]] and [[Hagfish|hagfish]], have no paired fins and no identifiable stomach, and they are ectothermic with a cartilaginous skeleton. The oldest fossil agnathans date from the [[Cambrian]], and armored forms known as ostracoderms were most diverse in the Early Devonian. Jawed vertebrates, or gnathostomes, evolved from jawless ancestors in the early [[Silurian]], and by the end of the Devonian all non-cyclostome jawless fish other than conodonts had become extinct. Hagfish are still counted among vertebrates because they secondarily lost their vertebrae, and they defend themselves by producing copious slime.

Indonesian singer, songwriter and actress. Born in [[Jakarta]], she was a child singer in the 1990s and became an Indonesian pop star in the 2000s. Her international career began in the mid-2010s with English-language albums and singles, including "Coke Bottle" with Timbaland and T.I. and "Overdose" with [[Chris Brown]]. She is the most-awarded Indonesian artist in history. In 2025 she was cast as Lila Hoth in the American series *Reacher*.

Position that suspends judgment on the existence of God or the divine. It is often characterized as an informed indecision by someone who has considered the question without reaching a conclusion. Agnosticism contrasts with [[Theism|theism]], which affirms God's existence, and [[Atheism|atheism]], which denies it. Strong agnosticism holds that God's existence is unknowable, while weak agnosticism holds that it is currently unknown. The term was coined in the 19th century by [[Thomas Henry Huxley]], who rejected conclusions drawn without sufficient evidence. Agnostic theists believe in God while denying that true knowledge of the divine is possible.

Anxiety disorder marked by fear of situations perceived as unsafe, where escape may be difficult. Such situations include public transit, crowds and queues, and being outside the home alone, and they may provoke panic attacks. Classified in the DSM-5 as a [[Phobia|phobia]], it is believed to result from genetic and environmental factors and often runs in families. Without treatment it rarely resolves, and cognitive behavioral therapy resolves it for about half of people. Women are affected about twice as often as men.

Angolan revolutionary, poet and politician, first president of Angola (1975–79). He led the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) during the war for independence from [[Portugal]], and was arrested several times for his activism while studying medicine there. After escaping from prison in 1960, he led the armed struggle against colonial rule. He led the MPLA at the start of the [[Angolan Civil War]], which began in 1975 and lasted until 2002. Considered Angola's preeminent poet, he wrote several books, and his birthday is celebrated as National Heroes' Day, a public holiday.

City on the Yamuna River in Uttar Pradesh, India, and former capital of the [[Mughal Empire]]. Under emperors Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, Agra was the foremost city of the Indian subcontinent and a center of learning, arts, commerce and religion. Shah Jahan built the [[Taj Mahal]] in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, completed in 1648; the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort are [[UNESCO]] World Heritage Sites. After the decline of the Mughal empire the city passed to the Marathas and then to the [[East India Company]]. Since independence Agra has developed as an industrial and tourist center, known for footwear and leather, and it lies on India's Golden Triangle tourist circuit with Delhi and Jaipur.

Multidisciplinary field of biology that applies exact, natural, economic and social sciences to agriculture. Its research includes improving productivity, such as developing drought-resistant crops and new [[Pesticide|pesticides]], and minimizing the effects of weeds, insects, pathogens and nematodes on crop and animal production. In the United States, the Hatch Act of 1887 marked the start of a scientific approach to agriculture. Recent work addresses [[Climate change|climate change]], which has made weather patterns less predictable and increased the frequency of droughts, floods and heatwaves; climate-smart strategies aim to adapt farming to these changes while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Practitioners are called agricultural scientists or agriculturists, and the field is closely related to [[Agronomy|agronomy]].

Sub-discipline of plant agriculture concerned with crop production and soil management, particularly for field crops under intensive farming. It applies biology, chemistry, economics, ecology, earth science and [[Genetics|genetics]]. Plant breeding has raised crop yields and improved the nutritional value of corn, soybeans and [[Wheat|wheat]]; triticale, a hybrid of rye and wheat, contains more usable protein than either parent. Agronomists analyze soils for [[Nitrogen|nitrogen]], [[Phosphorus|phosphorus]], [[Potassium|potassium]] and other nutrients, and develop methods such as contour plowing and no-till farming to prevent erosion. Agroecology, closely associated with sustainable agriculture, manages farming systems with an emphasis on ecological and environmental applications.

Ruler who founded the Durrani Empire and is often regarded as the founder of modern Afghanistan. Born into the Abdali tribe of Pashtuns and a commander under [[Nader Shah]], he was crowned near [[Kandahar]] after Nader's assassination in 1747 led to the breakup of the Afsharid Empire. Over 25 years he fought over fifteen major campaigns across West Asia, Central Asia and South Asia. From 1748 he invaded the [[Mughal Empire]], sacked [[Delhi]] in 1757 and annihilated Maratha armies at the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761. His campaigns also brought massacres, pillaging and mass enslavement, and contributed to the decline of Muslim power in northern India. He is buried in Kandahar.

Sultan of Morocco from 1578 to 1603 and the sixth and most famous ruler of the Saadi dynasty. He succeeded his brother Abd al-Malik, who died fighting the Portuguese at Ksar el-Kebir in 1578, and used ransoms from captured Portuguese to fill the royal treasury. He commissioned the El Badi Palace in [[Marrakesh]], finished in 1593 or 1594, and sought gold from the trans-Saharan trade of the [[Songhai Empire]]. In 1600 he sent an envoy to Queen [[Elizabeth I]] of [[England]] to negotiate an alliance against Spain. He was described as a man of profound Islamic learning who loved books, calligraphy and mathematics.

Arab jurist and founder of the Hanbali school of jurisprudence. Widely recognized as the scholar who memorized more [[Hadith|hadith]] than any other in Islamic history, he compiled *al-Musnad*, one of the largest hadith collections, which shaped the methods later used in *Sahih Bukhari* and *Sahih Muslim*. During the Mihna, a policy of the [[Abbasid Caliphate|Abbasid]] caliph al-Ma'mun that enforced the doctrine that the [[Quran]] was created, he refused to endorse that view and suffered physical persecution, a stance that made him a revered figure in traditional [[Sunni Islam|Sunni]] thought. His influence is debated: the Wahhabi reform movement has cited him as a principal influence, while some scholars argue that his own beliefs differ from Wahhabi doctrine.

[[Imam]] of the Adal Sultanate (1527–1543) who led its invasion and conquest of Abyssinia. Known in Amharic as Grañ and in Somali as Gurey, both meaning the left-handed, he won nearly all of his battles against the [[Ethiopian Empire|Ethiopians]] before 1541, including the Battle of Amba Sel, after which Emperor Dawit II was never again in a position to offer a pitched battle. The orientalist Frederick A. Edwards dubbed him the African Attila. He was defeated after a Portuguese intervention drew his war into a wider struggle between the Portuguese and the [[Ottoman Empire]]. His invasion remains part of the memory of both modern [[Ethiopia]] and Somalia.

Islamic messianic movement founded in British India on March 23, 1889, by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. Adherents, known as Ahmadi Muslims, believe Ahmad was the promised [[Messiah]] and Mahdi, who restored Islam to the precepts practised by [[Muhammad]] and the early Muslim community. The movement is led by a caliph. Mainstream Muslims regard Ahmad's claim to prophethood as heretical, and Ahmadis have faced non-recognition and persecution in many parts of the world. A small group, the Lahore Ahmadiyya Movement, split from the community over Ahmad's prophetic status.

Syrian statesman and former rebel commander, president of Syria since 2025. Also known by his former nom de guerre Abu Mohammad al-Julani, he founded Jabhat al-Nusra in 2012 with the support of [[Al-Qaeda|al-Qaeda]] and cut its ties with that group in 2016, later leading Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham. An 11-day offensive launched in November 2024 captured [[Damascus]] and toppled the [[Bashar al-Assad|Assad]] regime. He was formally appointed president on January 29, 2025. Massacres of Alawites in coastal Syria in the first year of his presidency involved government-affiliated troops.

Most populous city in the Indian state of [[Gujarat]], on the Sabarmati River. Its population was 5,570,585 at the 2011 census. Historically known as Karnavati, it was renamed after Ahmad Shah I of the Gujarat Sultanate, who transferred the capital there in 1411. The city is the second-largest producer of [[Cotton|cotton]] in India and, with [[Kanpur]], was known as the Manchester of India. Ahmedabad is an important economic, industrial and cultural hub, and [[Cricket|cricket]] is popular: the Narendra Modi Stadium at Motera seats 132,000 and is the largest stadium in the world. The city will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games. The historic city, or Old Ahmedabad, was declared a [[UNESCO]] World Heritage Site in 2017.
